sources.title: NGSS 3-LS1-1: Develop models to describe that organisms have unique and diverse life cycles
Natural History Museum: Frogspawn, tadpoles and froglets

legend.name: Tadpole
legend.meaning: Dark brown, for hiding on pond bottoms

legend.name: Egg jelly
legend.meaning: Clear jelly around each black embryo

steps.title: Eggs
steps.instruction: Trace the clump of frog eggs.

note.text: Stage 1. A frog lays hundreds or even thousands of eggs in water, in a clump of jelly called frogspawn. The jelly protects them.

steps.title: Embryos
steps.instruction: Draw the dark embryo in the middle of each egg.

note.text: Each black dot is an embryo. It feeds on its yolk and hatches as a tadpole in 1 to 4 weeks, faster in warm water.

steps.title: Tadpole
steps.instruction: Trace the tadpole's body and tail.

note.text: Stage 2. A tadpole lives underwater, breathes with gills, and swims with its tail. It eats algae.
note.remember: Tadpoles are fish-like: gills and a tail.

note.text: Its eyes are on the sides of its head, helping it watch for predators all around.

steps.title: Froglet
steps.instruction: Trace the froglet's body and shrinking tail.

note.text: Stage 3. Legs grow, back legs first. Lungs form, and the tail shrinks as the body absorbs it.
note.remember: A froglet is half tadpole, half frog.

steps.title: Froglet legs
steps.instruction: Draw the froglet's eye and its new legs.

note.text: With legs and lungs, a froglet can climb out of the water and breathe air for the first time.

steps.title: Adult frog
steps.instruction: Trace the adult frog's body and eyes.

note.text: Stage 4. The adult lives on land and in water. It breathes with lungs and through its skin, and eats insects.
note.remember: Amphibian means “double life”: water, then land.

steps.title: Legs
steps.instruction: Draw the frog's long back legs and short front legs.

note.text: Long, strong back legs let a frog jump many times its body length to catch food and escape danger.

steps.title: The cycle
steps.instruction: Draw the arrows from stage to stage, going clockwise.

note.text: Adult frogs return to water to lay eggs, so the cycle starts again. The change from tadpole to frog is metamorphosis.

steps.title: Color
steps.instruction: These are simplified real colors. The egg jelly stays clear.

steps.title: Stage order
steps.instruction: Tap the stages in order, starting from the egg.
steps.why: The egg hatches into a tadpole, which grows legs and lungs as a froglet, then becomes an adult that lays eggs.
steps.hint: Which stage has gills and lives only in water?

steps.title: Label the stages
steps.instruction: Pick the right name for each numbered stage.

targets.role: Laid in water, protected by jelly.
Lives underwater and breathes with gills.

mistakes.Froglet: A froglet has legs. This one has only a tail, so it's a tadpole.

targets.role: Has legs and lungs, but still a short tail.

mistakes.Tadpole: Look at the legs: tadpoles don't have any yet. This is a froglet.

commonMistakes.Pupa: Frogs have no pupa stage. They change gradually, growing legs while still swimming.
commonMistakes.Chrysalis: A chrysalis belongs to butterflies. Frogs change gradually, without one.

steps.title: Explain
steps.question: Why does a tadpole have gills, while an adult frog has lungs?

options.text: Tadpoles live underwater; adult frogs also live on land and breathe air
options.feedback: Yes. Gills take oxygen from water, and lungs take it from air. The frog's body changes as its home changes.
Tadpoles swim with their tails. Gills are for breathing underwater.
Jumping uses the strong back legs. Lungs are for breathing air.

options.text: Adult frogs never go in water
options.feedback: Many adult frogs spend lots of time in water, and they return to it to lay eggs.
